title: Diameter of Binary Tree
statement: Given the level-order array representation of a binary tree, return the diameter: the number of edges on the longest path between any two nodes in the tree.

examples.explanation: The longest path is 4 -> 2 -> 1 -> 3, which uses 3 edges.

hints: For node index i, children sit at 2*i + 1 and 2*i + 2 in the level-order array.
The longest path through a node equals leftHeight + rightHeight (in edges).
Track the global best across all nodes while returning 1 + max(left, right) upward.

solutions.title: All-Pairs Path Check
Single Postorder Pass

editorial.approach: The diameter is the length of the longest path between any two nodes, which may or may not pass through the root. Compute the max depth of each subtree recursively using post-order DFS. At each node, the longest path passing through that node is left_depth + right_depth. Update a global maximum diameter at each node, while returning 1 + max(left_depth, right_depth) to the caller.
editorial.why_optimal: Visits each node in the tree exactly once in O(N) time with O(H) call stack space, computing height and path length simultaneously in a bottom-up pass.
editorial.pitfalls: Confusing the count of nodes on the path with the count of edges (diameter is measured in edges, so a single node has diameter 0). Assuming the diameter must pass through the tree root.
